title: Fast fallback matrix for routing refactor — personal memo
content:
Context:
This is a quick, messy brain dump to capture the fallback and revert options we should wire up for the routing-layer refactor (split reader/writer paths + optimized prefix cache). Intended for pair-review with Jun and a short runbook for on-call during rollout windows. Keep it lean — focus on safe fast-fail paths and metrics to watch.

Goals:
- Make it possible to degrade with <=1 configuration flip to preserve availability.
- Have automated traffic split and two-step canary to limit blast radius.
- Ensure observable signals map cleanly to a revert decision within 5–10 minutes.

Quick decision matrix (TL;DR):
- Severe functional errors (500s for core routes): immediate full rollback to v_prev, notify pager.
- Latency inflation (>95 p50 up 2x, p95 up 1.5x): throttle new path (route-level) -> reduce batch sizes -> if persists rollback.
- Memory pressure on GPU hosts: route steering to cheaper model variant + decrease batch/ttl -> if OOM continue, rollback.
- Quality regressions (rerank/LLM hallucination delta): pause new model variant, route to stable model, open eval job.

Automatable controls to implement before next canary:
- Per-route traffic gate: percentage split via config flag (config service + runtime override).
- Emergency toggle endpoint: /admin/route-fallback?route=xxx&mode=legacy (authz-limited).
- Canary auto-unwind: if p95 latency increases > X% for 3 consecutive windows -> auto-switch back.
- Metric shadowing: always send to both paths but only count new-path latency/err for canary fraction.

Checklist for PR reviewers (what I want eyes on):
- Config churn: ensure new flags have sane defaults and clear migration comments.
- Observability hooks: are we emitting route_id, variant_id, fallback_reason and kv-cache-hit tags? Missing tags block fast diagnosis.
- Idempotency: verify requests retried across routing decisions remain safe (no double side-effects).
- Timeout boundaries: confirm client vs internal timeouts; new path should have slightly lower internal timeout to favor graceful fallback.
- Test coverage: unit + integration mocks for both legacy and refactored path. Add one e2e with simulated slow backend.
- Rollout docs updated: console toggles, SRE runbook, and cost estimate (because batch changes affect token costs).

Manual QA scenarios (pair with Jun):
- Scenario A: path latency spike -> simulate 3x p95 by injecting sleep in cache layer -> expect traffic gate to reduce to 0% after configured threshold.
- Scenario B: KV cache miss storm -> inject key-churn -> observe CPU/IO on serving hosts and verify fallback to less cache-dependent variant.
- Scenario C: Partial auth failure -> fail token introspection for 10% of requests -> ensure failures are isolated and not escalating.

Rollback quick-run (playbook for on-call):
1) Run /admin/route-fallback?route=<name>&mode=legacy (or flip named config in config service).
2) Reduce traffic weight to 0 for new path in traffic-split control plane.
3) If memory/CPU issues: drain affected nodes, scale up legacy pool if needed.
4) Post-mortem: capture 15m windows of traces, top 10 request ids, and a diff of config snapshots.

Metrics to watch (dashboard widgets):
- p50/p95 latency per route and per-path (legacy vs new).
- 5m error rate per route (5xx and 4xx), and error type breakdown.
- KV-cache hit ratio and avg TTL per keyspace.
- GPU utilization and host OOM counts.
- Model quality delta: normalized BLEU/QA-score on cherry prompts (near-real time evals).

Edge cases and questions to resolve (TODOs):
- Can we reuse existing traffic-split controller or need a new lightweight API? (open: RUNT-6743)
- Should the emergency toggle be an orchestration runbook only, or also UI in Console? Risk: too many toggles in Console causes accidental flips.
- How to version telemetry so old dashboards still display meaningful comparison? Plan: emit variant_label + canary_id.
- Who owns post-rollback automation? Ops or dev team? Decide in next triage.

Notes to self (implementation hints):
- Keep the batching changes behind feature-flag; new batcher needs fallback to "preserve-order=false" path to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Add small synthetic load generator job that runs during canary to surface perf regressions quickly.
- Attach a small smoke test to the PR that runs against local emulators (no real GPUs) to catch obvious NPEs.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Pair with Jun to add metric tags and the quick toggle endpoint (target: 2-day spike).
- Draft the SRE one-pager for the Friday canary window (Sophie to review).
- Wire PR #8421 with these checks and mark for lightweight canary after green e2e.

Unresolved assumptions:
- We assume model variant fallbacks are compatible (same input/output contract). If not, will need compatibility shim.
- Cost impact of smaller batches vs extra calls needs sign-off from finance for large customers.

If anyone reads: this is intentionally terse — flag anything unclear and Ill expand.
